name: Y Combinator
blurb: The startup school behind Airbnb, Stripe, Reddit and Dropbox, now in an old shipyard office.
lore: Paul Graham, Jessica Livingston, Robert Tappan Morris and Trevor Blackwell started Y Combinator in March 2005, running batches in Cambridge, Massachusetts and Mountain View. Its first class included Reddit, and later batches produced Dropbox, Airbnb and Stripe. After 17 years in Mountain View it moved to Dogpatch, into 560 20th Street, a brick building put up as the office of Union Iron Works, the shipyard that became Bethlehem Steel.
facts: YC's second building, 580 20th Street, once housed compressors that powered the shipyard's air tools.
In 2018 a glitch accepted, then rejected, about 15,000 Startup School applicants. YC then accepted all of them.
Gusto and Astranis, both YC alumni, work in the brick buildings across the street.

name: Andreessen Horowitz
blurb: The venture firm known as a16z. Its main office is Menlo Park, this is its SF outpost.
lore: Marc Andreessen and Ben Horowitz had been angel investors together for years before founding the firm in 2009 with a $300 million first fund. Its headquarters is on Sand Hill Road in Menlo Park, outside this map. In 2019 it signed for its San Francisco office at 180 Townsend Street in China Basin, which its own offices page still lists.
facts: a16z is a numeronym: 16 letters sit between the A of Andreessen and the z of Horowitz.
Its first investment was Skype, which Microsoft bought in 2011 for $8.5 billion.
Its $100 million bet on GitHub in 2012 returned over $1 billion when Microsoft bought GitHub.

name: Founders, Inc.
blurb: A 42,000 square foot founder campus on the Fort Mason waterfront.
lore: Founders, Inc. started in 2020 and runs a 42,000 square foot campus in Building C at Fort Mason, with hardware labs and a media studio. It writes first checks of $100,000 to $250,000 into early teams in AI, AR and VR, hardware and robotics, and opens its campus for hack nights and open house evenings.
facts: Its Night Hack gives builders five hours to make hardware or software, with live demos only.
Portfolio companies include LiveKit and thirdweb.
Fort Mason Center opened its old Army buildings to the public in 1977.

name: Founders Fund
blurb: We wanted flying cars. The Presidio venture firm behind SpaceX's first check.
lore: Peter Thiel, Ken Howery and Luke Nosek founded Founders Fund in 2005. It was the first institutional investor in SpaceX and Palantir and an early backer of Facebook. The firm works out of One Letterman Drive in the Presidio, on the same campus as Lucasfilm.
facts: Its manifesto once carried the line: We wanted flying cars, instead we got 140 characters.
In 2018 the firm reportedly returned $4.60 per dollar invested.

name: General Catalyst
blurb: A Cambridge venture firm with a 20th floor perch on Hawthorne Street.
lore: Joel Cutler and David Fialkow founded General Catalyst in Massachusetts in 2000. It backed Airbnb, Stripe, Anthropic and Samsara, and its San Francisco office is on the 20th floor of 75 Hawthorne Street.
facts: General Catalyst bought Summa Health, an Ohio hospital network, for $485 million.
The firm is still headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts.

name: Greylock
blurb: One of the oldest venture firms, high up in the old phone company tower.
lore: Bill Elfers and Dan Gregory founded Greylock in Cambridge, Massachusetts in 1965, one of the oldest venture firms still investing. It moved its headquarters to Silicon Valley in 2009 and backed Facebook, Zynga and Flickr. Its San Francisco office is Suite 2600 at 140 New Montgomery, the old Pacific Telephone building.
facts: LinkedIn co-founder Reid Hoffman is a Greylock partner.
Benchmark also lists 140 New Montgomery as its headquarters, and Yelp used to work here too.

name: Benchmark
blurb: Five equal partners, no CEO, and the eBay bet of the century.
lore: Bob Kagle, Bruce Dunlevie, Andy Rachleff, Kevin Harvey and Val Vaden founded Benchmark in 1995. Its partners own the firm equally, with no senior or junior ranks. In 2012 it leased space above the Warfield on Market Street, and it now lists 140 New Montgomery as its headquarters.
facts: In 1997 Benchmark paid $6.7 million for 22.1% of eBay.
It put $12 million into Uber in 2011 for an 11% stake.
Benchmark partners show up as characters in the TV dramas WeCrashed and Super Pumped.

name: Lightspeed
blurb: Snapchat's first venture investor, on historic South Park.
lore: Barry Eggers, Christopher Schaepe, Ravi Mhatre and Peter Nieh, who had studied at Stanford together, founded Lightspeed in 2000. It led early rounds in Nest and MuleSoft, and in 2012 became Snapchat's first venture investor. Its San Francisco office is at 2 South Park.
facts: Lightspeed was Snap's fourth-largest shareholder at its 2017 IPO.
Google bought Lightspeed-backed Nest for $3.2 billion.

name: Initialized Capital
blurb: A seed fund started by a Reddit co-founder and two YC alumni.
lore: Alexis Ohanian, Harj Taggar and Garry Tan founded Initialized Capital in 2011 to write early checks into software startups. Its San Francisco office is listed at 464 Tehama Street in SoMa.
facts: Co-founder Alexis Ohanian also co-founded Reddit in Y Combinator's first batch.

name: 500 Global
blurb: Formerly 500 Startups, an accelerator that backed thousands of companies.
lore: Dave McClure and Christine Tsai founded 500 Startups in 2010 and renamed it 500 Global in 2021. It invested in more than 2,400 companies by 2021. Its San Francisco space took the entire sixth floor of 814 Mission Street.
facts: The firm runs VC Unlocked, a course that teaches people how to be investors.

name: Redpoint
blurb: Raised the biggest debut fund of its day, now on Maiden Lane.
lore: Redpoint was founded in 1999 by investors behind Juniper Networks and Netflix and raised a $600 million first fund, the largest first-time fund for a new firm at the time. It backed Snowflake, Twilio and Stripe. Its San Francisco office is listed at 27 Maiden Lane off Union Square.
facts: Redpoint counts more than 130 IPOs and acquisitions among its companies.

name: Index Ventures
blurb: A Geneva venture firm that opened a San Francisco office in 2011.
lore: Neil Rimer, David Rimer and Giuseppe Zocco founded Index Ventures in Geneva in 1996. It opened a San Francisco office in 2011 and is listed at 139 Townsend Street, a block from Andreessen Horowitz.
facts: In 2016 Index spun its life sciences business out as Medicxi.
Index raised $3.1 billion across new funds in 2021.
